articles.title: Travis Kalanick is back: How Uber’s ousted founder went from pariah to Silicon Valley hero
articles.summary: The Uber cofounder returns with a multibillion robotics and AI venture—and a tech sector more receptive to his hard-charging approach.
articles.body:
In 2017, it looked as if the tech world had seen the last of Travis Kalanick. Following a spate of scandals and allegations ranging from sexism to corporate espionage, Uber's own investors took the extraordinary step of forcing the CEO out of the firm he cofounded .

Kalanick's ouster also signaled a bigger cultural shift. As the epilogue of Super Pumped , the definitive account of Uber's chaotic early days by tech journalist Mike Isaac, put it: "Change had indeed come to the Valley. With the fading of characters like … Kalanick, the backslapping bro culture of Silicon Valley's aught era is now seen as passé."

That may have felt true in 2019, when the book was released, but since then much has changed. Now, after nearly a decade of self-imposed exile, Travis Kalanick is back—not contrite, not chastened, and not especially interested in accepting his critics' moral verdict on his tenure at Uber.

It seems to be working for him. He has a multibillion-dollar industrial robotics venture , the backing of a powerful new set of patrons, and an increasingly receptive audience of young founders who see his downfall as less a reckoning than a cautionary tale about what happens when Silicon Valley lets investors, journalists, and cultural politics constrain its most forceful builders. Nearly a decade after Uber's board pushed him out, Kalanick is seen by his admirers as a victim of "corporate cancel culture," a founder who was unjustly removed before he could finish the job.

In a recent series of video appearances, Kalanick doesn't seem to have changed much. His hair and beard are gray, and there are new lines in his handsome face, but his affect is the same: charismatic and hypercompetitive, with intense dark eyes that can convey both charm and menace.

Since his ouster, Kalanick has acquired legendary status among a new crop of up-and-coming founders. Some go so far as to compare him to another iconoclast who was forced out of his own company. "He's the Steve Jobs for founders of my generation," says Kush Bavaria, who has raised $33 million for his AI data startup Ornn. Bavaria added that young entrepreneurs revere Kalanick for notching the rarest of achievements—building a company like Google or Airbnb whose name has become a verb.

Many in Silicon Valley's VC establishment are offering Kalanick a full-throated welcome back into the sunshine, too. "It takes a rare kind of entrepreneur to change these old-school, heavy parts of our economy," Ben Horowitz—whose influential venture capital firm, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), is backing Kalanick's company, Atoms—wrote in a recent blog post. "Travis is that guy."

articles.title: Tesla finally moves to electrify trucking
articles.summary: Tesla's Semi truck, with a 500-mile range, is about to hit the road in big numbers, with the company saying it plans to make 50,000 units a year.
articles.body:
Tesla is finally handing over the first of its all-electric Semi trucks to customers after nearly a decade of delays and refinements to the vehicle, which it first revealed in 2017.

Company executives — except CEO Elon Musk, who was at President Trump's state dinner with Chinese Premier Xi Jinping — walked an audience of customers, employees, and influencers through many of the details at an event in Reno, Nevada, on Thursday night.

Customers will be able to take delivery of the truck whenever they are ready, though charging infrastructure remains a hurdle, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch on the condition of anonymity.

Without revealing the final sticker price, the executives promised the truck will help fleet owners lower their total cost of ownership, reduce emissions, and benefit from greater reliability.

The event was held at a new factory dedicated to the Semi that's adjacent to the company's first Gigafactory in Reno. Tesla plans to build as many as 50,000 trucks a year at the plant, or roughly 1,000 per week, and create 3,000 jobs for the local economy. The most capable version of the truck is expected to travel 500 miles or more on one charge (depending on the size of the load) and cost just shy of $300,000 before incentives. There will be shorter-range variants, too.

The Semi's long-awaited launch comes at a time of transition for Tesla. Musk now paints Tesla as a robotics and AI company even though nearly all of its revenue comes from vehicle sales. He has also changed Tesla's mission to "build a world of amazing abundance." When he showed off the Semi in 2017, Tesla's mission was still "to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy."

Despite the change in positioning, and seemingly priorities for Tesla, Thursday's event still saw a lot of discussion about reducing trucking emissions. Dan Priestley, the head of Tesla's Semi program, noted that heavy trucks produce 16% of emissions despite making up just 1% of vehicles on the road.

"We're super excited to be deploying these into our own operations because it's fulfilling the mission that we originally started out [with]," he said.

"Occasionally we get a little too far out there"

Originally slated to go into production in 2019, the Semi was delayed for multiple reasons. The pandemic, a global parts supply and semiconductor shortage, and changes made in response to pilot customer feedback all contributed to the years-long wait.

Priestley and Lars Moravy, who leads most of Tesla's engineering efforts, detailed many of those changes during the 30-minute event — timed thus to show a Semi that started at 3% battery go up to 60% while plugged into one of Tesla's megawatt charging stations. (Tesla is also building an entire network of these chargers, which Priestley detailed during the event.)

articles.title: Kroger pulls a gas perk as pump prices set a September record
articles.summary: The switch happens automatically, so many won’t notice until they’re at the pump.
articles.body:
At a time when gas prices have hit seasonal record highs, Kroger has ended a partnership that will take away a key gas discount from customers.

And while the move was announced in July, it's actually hitting now, when Kroger customers arguably need it most.

"The national average for a gallon of regular gasoline continues to climb, up nearly 5 cents from last week. At $4.48 per gallon, this is the highest the national average has ever been for this time of year," AAA reported on Sept. 24.

That's not a situation Kroger could have predicted in July, when it shared that its relationship with U.S. Bank was ending. This meant the Kroger Elite Mastercard, along with the benefits that come with it, would be terminated.

"U.S. Bank will transition credit card clients with The Kroger Co. co-brand credit card to a U.S. Bank Smartly Visa card, with U.S. Bank maintaining account ownership, servicing, and ongoing client relationships," the bank shared on its website .

The new card is not affiliated with Kroger and does not come with the gas savings and other benefits the former co-branded card offered. U.S. Bank said the change "is expected to be completed this fall."

It's now fall, and Kroger customers are losing a key gas savings at a very unfortunate time.

Kroger credit card holders lose a gas benefit

Kroger shared more information on the credit card closure on its website , and not all the news was bad.

"Your Kroger loyalty account will remain active, and you will continue to earn Kroger loyalty points on eligible purchases when using your Kroger loyalty account number. Any earned Kroger loyalty points can still be redeemed for fuel discounts or grocery savings," it posted.

Still, cardholders will lose a generous gas perk.

"However, your current 5¢ per gallon fuel savings at Kroger Fuel Centers associated with the Kroger World Elite Mastercard will end when your credit card account is converted or closed," Kroger shared.

That benefit allowed all cardholders to save 5 cents per gallon, but grew to 25 cents per gallon for members who spent $6,000 a year on the credit card. In addition, to redeem the added discount, cardholders needed to redeem at least 100 fuel points.

If you spent $6,000 on the card in the previous year, you got the 25 cents per gallon discount. That means a savings of $2.50 for every 10-gallon fill-up.

Anyone below the $6,000 threshold received the 5-cent benefit, giving them a more modest $0.50 savings for that same fill-up.

articles.title: Temporal deixa 3 famílias desalojadas e provoca 25 ocorrências no AC | G1
articles.standfirst: Chamados foram registrados em 14 bairros após chuva de quase 80 milímetros em menos de duas horas na última sexta (25). Famílias estão em casas de parentes.
articles.summary: Chamados foram registrados em 14 bairros após chuva de quase 80 milímetros em menos de duas horas na última sexta-feira (25). Famílias estão em casas de parentes.
articles.body:
Três famílias dos bairros da Paz, Esperança e Tancredo Neves precisaram deixar as próprias casas após o temporal que atingiu Rio Branco na noite da última sexta-feira (25) e estão abrigadas em casas de parentes.

Segundo a Defesa Civil Municipal, cerca de 10 a 11 pessoas estão nessa situação. Também foram registradas 25 ocorrências relacionadas à chuva , com situações mais graves em 14 bairros da capital .

👉 Contexto: O temporal ocorreu após um período de chuva intensa que acumulou quase 80 milímetros em menos de duas horas . O volume corresponde a cerca de 88% da média esperada para todo o mês de setembro , que é de aproximadamente 92,6 milímetros.

Segundo o coordenador da Defesa Civil de Rio Branco , tenente-coronel Cláudio Falcão, entre os chamados estão alagamentos e quedas de árvores.

Chuva forte provocou alagamentos, quedas de árvores e desabamentos em diferentes pontos de Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo/Defesa Civil de Rio Branco

"Se dividir as ocorrências, foram registrados principalmente queda de árvores sobre residência, alagamentos, desmoronamento, risco de desabamento, queda de torre e queda de árvore em via pública", explicou.

Moradores chegaram a registrar a força da tempestade e os prejuízos provocados em diferentes regiões da cidade. No bairro Caladinho, uma moradora mostrou a casa inundada após a água entrar no imóvel.

No Lago do Amor, comerciantes da Feira da Economia Solidária também tiveram prejuízos. Barracas foram derrubadas pela força do vento, enquanto objetos e produtos ficaram molhados. ( Veja vídeo abaixo )

A Universidade Federal do Acre (Ufac) e bairros do entorno, como Tucumã, Rui Lino e Mocinha Magalhães, também registraram queda de energia. Em diferentes regiões da capital, ruas ficaram alagadas e com dificuldades para o trânsito.

Segundo Falcão, o grande volume de chuva concentrado em um intervalo de menos de duas horas foi um dos fatores que contribuíram para os alagamentos.

"O que mais preocupa nessa situação é o tempo que choveu, foi menos de duas horas, então uma quantidade muito elevada de chuva e de pluviometria para pouco tempo. Isso não tem jeito, não tem cidade, não tem drenagem que resista, vai causar alagamentos", afirmou.

O coordenador da Defesa Civil também chamou atenção para o comportamento das chuvas neste mês.

Segundo Falcão, o volume e a intensidade registrados em setembro estão fora do padrão esperado para o período , o que dificulta a previsão e a preparação das equipes.

Alagamentos atingiram um bar na Rua Isaura Parente em apenas 10 minutos de chuva — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Ele explicou que o sistema de alertas envolve as defesas civis municipal, estadual e federal. No caso do temporal de sexta, o município recebeu um aviso do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), por meio da Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente (Sema), mas, segundo Falcão, o alerta chegou quando a chuva já havia começado.

"2026 tem sido totalmente atípico. As previsões ficam muito difíceis de ser concretizadas, porque está totalmente fora do padrão climático que a gente tem todos os anos. Precisamos aprimorar sim, precisamos nos voltar para essa questão de alertas, de alerta à população, mas em tempo hábil, para que a população possa se proteger e ter seu autocuidado", afirmou.

Além disso, o nível do Rio Acre também apresentou oscilação entre o sábado (26) e este domingo (27).

Conforme o boletim da Defesa Civil Municipal, o manancial estava em 2,17 metros às 5h17 de sábado e marcou 1,75 metro às 5h16 deste domingo, uma redução de 42 centímetros em cerca de 24 horas.

O boletim deste domingo não registrou chuva nas últimas 24 horas. Portanto, no sábado o acumulado informado foi de 70,6 milímetros.

Rio Acre marcou 1,75 metros na manhã deste domingo (27) em Rio Branco — Foto: De olho no rio/Prefeitura de Rio Branco

A previsão é de continuidade das chuvas. A Defesa Civil orienta os moradores a redobrar a atenção em áreas sujeitas a alagamentos, desabamentos e quedas de árvores.

A população também pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199 ou o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

Há alerta para possíveis problemas na rede elétrica. A Energisa informou que mantém equipes mobilizadas para atender ocorrências durante o período de chuva.

A concessionária orienta a população a permanecer em local seguro, retirar aparelhos eletrônicos das tomadas e não se aproximar de cabos rompidos.

Em caso de ocorrência, os chamados podem ser feitos pelo aplicativo Energisa On, pelo WhatsApp Gisa, no número (68) 99233-0341, ou pelo telefone 0800 647 7196.

articles.title: Cury diz que bets devem ser eliminadas ou taxadas em até 60% | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Avante à Presidência da República cumpriu agenda em Belo Horizonte neste domingo (27). Ele defendeu mudanças na área econômica, investimentos em saúde e educação e voltou a criticar plataformas de apostas online.
articles.summary: Candidato do Avante à Presidência da República cumpriu agenda em Belo Horizonte neste domingo (27). Ele defendeu mudanças na área econômica, investimentos em saúde e educação e voltou a criticar plataformas de apostas online.
articles.body:
O candidato do Avante à Presidência da República, Augusto Cury , cumpriu agenda de campanha em Belo Horizonte neste domingo (27). Durante uma visita à Praça do Papa, ele afirmou que as plataformas de apostas esportivas, conhecidas como bets, deveriam ser eliminadas ou submetidas a uma taxação maior ( veja vídeo acima ).

"As bets precisam ser enquadradas: ou elas têm que ser eliminadas ou têm que ser taxadas como cigarro, porque dão dependência, e grave. Então, têm que ser taxadas em 50% a 60% para que possamos evitar que elas se propaguem de maneira cruel", destacou o presidenciável.

A declaração de Cury foi feita dois dias após o presidente Lula (PT) anunciar uma MP que proíbe sites e aplicativos de apostas a partir de 6 de outubro no país . Até às 23h59 do dia 5, os apostadores poderão retirar os valores mantidos nas plataformas ( leia mais aqui ).

Ao comentar sobre a formação de um eventual governo, o candidato disse que pretende convidar especialistas de diferentes áreas para compor a equipe ministerial e defendeu uma gestão baseada em critérios técnicos.

Cury também afirmou que pretende investir em políticas de proteção às mulheres, valorização dos professores, mudanças nos currículos escolares e ampliação do acesso à saúde pública.

Além disso, defendeu a expansão do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) e a criação de uma rede de telemedicina para acelerar atendimentos, especialmente em regiões mais vulneráveis.

"Nós vamos ter um SUS turbinado, os médicos serão valorizados, o corpo de enfermeiros, e vamos expandir o SUS", disse.

O presidenciável ainda falou sobre medidas para incentivar o empreendedorismo. Entre as propostas apresentadas, está a divisão do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) em duas estruturas, uma voltada para grandes empresas e outra para micro e pequenas empresas.

Augusto Cury (Avante) critica bets durante agenda de campanha em Belo Horizonte — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Renan Santos defende intervenção federal em estados  | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à presidência esteve em Salvador, neste domingo (27), em agenda de campanha. Em entrevista coletiva, ele colocou a segurança como um dos seus principais focos, caso eleito.
articles.summary: Candidato à presidência esteve em Salvador, neste domingo (27), em agenda de campanha. Em entrevista, ele colocou a segurança como um dos seus principais focos, caso eleito
articles.body:
Renan Santos defende intervenção federal em estados que não colaborarem no combate ao crime organizado — Foto: Reprodução/TV Bahia

O candidato à presidência do Brasil Renan Santos ( Missão ) defendeu, neste domingo (27), uma intervenção federal em estados que não colaborarem com medidas que pretende por em prática contra o crime organizado, caso seja eleito.

A declaração foi dada em coletiva de imprensa, durante visita a Salvador , em cumprimento de agenda de campanha com apoiadores. O ato aconteceu na frente da Reitoria da Universidade Federal da Bahia (Ufba), no Centro da cidade. Ele não detalhou como pretende agir.

"Eu quero colaborar com todos os governadores, não importa a cor ideológica, se é vermelho, se é azul, se é amarelo e preto. Agora, não colaborou, nós vamos meter uma interferência, uma intervenção no estado. Eu preciso dos governadores atuando conosco, ou o Governo Federal vai atuar", disse.

Na ocasião, o candidato defendeu a pauta da segurança pública como um dos principais pilares do seu governo, e citou o Nordeste como exemplo de região onde pretende combater a atuação de facções. Falou ainda da intenção de desenvolver a economia da região.

"O Nordeste tem dois problemas gravíssimos. Um é a dependência que as família têm de políticas existenciais e a outra é a destruição do tecido social por causa do crime organizado. De um lado, nós temos que levar desenvolvimento econômico, ou seja, vou cortar muita despesa do Governo Federal, para transformar em desenvolvimento e infraestrutura, que vai atuar muito na parte de energia, que tem um potencial gigantesco, e na destruição das facções, do crime", afirmou.

Quando questionado sobre a Bahia especificamente, Renan Santos alegou ter recebido ameaças após repercutir crimes ocorridos no estado.

"O que eu vi aqui na Bahia, porque eu já gravei vídeos aqui em Salvador, é que é humilhante para as pessoas que moram. As pessoas que moram nas comunidades vivem uma vida opressiva. O crime organizado não permite usar certas marcas de roupa. Quando eu vi, achei que era piada. Quando começaram a surgir os primeiros casos que a pessoa fazia um símbolo ou colocava uma roupa e era morta, eu falei: 'Ah, é exagero'. E não é. Eu recebi ameaças depois disso", destacou.

Afirmou também que membros de facções que não se entregarem ou forem presos e tentarem contra as forças policiais serão combatidos com rigor.

Em outro momento da entrevista, o candidato disse estar empenhado em chegar ao segundo turno e descartou apoiar Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ou Flávio Bolsonaro.

"Eu montei o meu partido para dar para mim, para ela, a opção de sermos candidatos. E, para todas essas pessoas aqui, a chance delas não precisarem votar em bandidos. (...) Eu vou trabalhar para ir para o segundo turno", pontuou.

Os dois candidatos foram alvos de crítica de Renan, que apontou suas relações e a relação de apoiadores nas investigações sobre o Banco Master.

"Indo em um debate, eles sabem, tendo espaço para mais de 40 milhões de brasileiros assistirem, é impossível o brasileiro dar o governo para um bandido envolvido no Caso Master, que recebeu dinheiro para fazer um filme, ou o outro bandido que está envolvido no Caso Master porque todo o partido dele, especialmente aqui na Bahia, está nesse mesmo escândalo", alegou.

O candidato também reforçou o posicionamento contrário às bets. "Nós vamos proibir todas as bets no Brasil. As bets se tornaram uma praga para lavagem de dinheiro, mesmo as legalizadas. Uma praga ligada ao endividamento e à destruição da cabeça dos brasileiros. Infelizmente, essa foi uma liberdade que foi trazida para as pessoas e que vem tornando as pessoas viciadas, vem fazendo mal".

E voltou a criticar a posição de Lula ao tomar decisões sobre o setor durante o período eleitoral . "Eu só não acho que deveria ter sido feito como o Lula fez, no período eleitoral e sem uma transição para grupos de mídia e times esportivos, que contavam com isso. Não houve uma transição. O Lula fez porque ele está querendo transformar isso em matéria eleitoral".

articles.title: With no heirs to leave it to, this billionaire is pouring his fortune into a Texas ghost town of about 25 people
articles.summary: John Poindexter, the 81-year-old founder of truck-body maker J.B. Poindexter & Co., wants to turn Shafter, Texas, into a living history museum.
articles.body:
The $124 trillion Great Wealth Transfer is underway , and baby boomers are passing down their fortunes to their heirs.

But what happens when an ultrawealthy person has no descendants?

In the case of 81-year-old billionaire John Poindexter , he's getting creative and funneling some of his wealth into a quite unexpected cause: a super small town in West Texas.

Shafter, Texas, is a ghost town in a county that just keeps getting emptier. Presidio County had an estimated 5,433 residents in 2025, down 11.4% since 2020 and down from 7,818 in 2010, Census Bureau data shows. The median household income is just $43,802 (about half the median U.S. income ), nearly one in five residents lives in poverty, and only about 1.6 people live per square mile.

But Poindexter, a Houston manufacturing magnate, is betting on it anyway. Since late 2020, his Tidewater and Big Bend Foundation has taken in nearly $67 million in contributions, according to IRS filings compiled by ProPublica . That includes $20.6 million in the fiscal year ending November 2024, when the foundation reported $62.5 million in net assets.

The foundation's signature project is Shafter, the former silver-mining town where about 25 people live, according to the Big Bend Sentinel . The plans, according to the Times , call for a resort and living history museum anchored by a rebuilt saloon, general store, and post office, with about a dozen adobe homes available for overnight rentals.

When the Times asked why his family won't inherit his wealth instead, Poindexter said: "I've never been married, I have no children." That's a different path from Warren Buffett, who has directed his $140 billion wealth to four of his family's foundations so they can choose how to spend it. With no children to hand the reins to, Poindexter is building his own. Poindexter's foundation will eventually own all of his properties, the Times reported, including the 30,000-acre Cibolo Creek Ranch where Justice Antonin Scalia died in 2016 .

Shafter's Presidio Mine operated from 1883 to 1942 and produced 35.2 million ounces of silver, according to Black Bear Minerals , which now owns it. After the mine closed, the town emptied out.

By early 2025, Poindexter had bought several Shafter properties and offered to restore the historic church at the town's entrance, the Big Bend Sentinel reported. Not every resident is sold on the plan, but a new restaurant and shop would likely be welcome. For now, the closest place to buy groceries is Presidio, which is 19 miles away. Shafter resident and water board president David Long told the Sentinel the preservation efforts could spur more people to move to the ghost town.

articles.title: 2 key checks for the AI trade and the economy: What to watch this week
articles.summary: Micron earnings and the September jobs report are set to lead market headlines this week.
articles.body:
Last week saw two big headlines dominate the conversation. First, the explosion of Meta's Muse and its wearable AI "Charm," then Chinese president Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington — both closely watched by investors for their implications on both the AI trade and the state of play between the world's two largest economies.

Nevertheless, they didn't do much to markets for the week, with stocks holding mostly steady despite all the headlines and market forces swirling around.

This week, however, will pivot back to the earnings calendar, with Wednesday having the biggest event.

Memory giant Micron ( MU ) reports fiscal fourth quarter earnings. After the waffling of the AI infrastructure trade over the past two weeks, investors will be looking for signs of continued demand in the memory trade, which has emerged as one of the most significant bottlenecks for the AI build-out.

Elsewhere in the calendar, Nike ( NKE ) reports on Thursday, where embattled CEO Elliott Hill will look to assuage concerns from investors that Nike has lost its spark. One thing that'll be hot on everyone's minds: French soccer star Kylian Mbappé's decision to leave Nike and join the team at On ( ON ), a tough loss for the American sportswear giant.

On the economic data front, it's jobs week! Last month's report of 162,000 jobs added in August — roughly three times expectations — has set a high bar for the September numbers, where economists are looking for 100,000 jobs added in Friday's report. Also on the calendar is PCE inflation data on Wednesday. As the Fed's preferred metric, the PCE data is set to be closely watched for a read on whether the FOMC will indeed hike rates again in 2026.

We have to hand it to them: Last week was Meta's week.

Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg laid out his vision for the company's future during its Meta Connect conference on Wednesday, and it's all about Muse .

The social media giant's new AI agent has quickly jumped to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store, and, according to Zuckerberg, millions of people are using it.

During Connect, Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang demonstrated a number of use cases for Muse, ranging from the mundane, like scheduling meetings, to more impressive feats like negotiating better rates for cable service and making purchases across multiple services.

Meta is also bringing Muse to its next-generation Meta VR Glasses , allowing you to speak to a digital avatar of your agent, as well as to its Muse Charm. A handheld, purpose-built device, the Muse Charm lets you interact with your Muse agent without a smartphone or smart glasses.

Stocks have been on a tear recently. The S&P 500 has repeatedly hit record highs over the past couple of months, despite concerns over geopolitical turmoil, rising bond yields and some U.S. economic policies.

Despite the S&P 500 being close to its all-time high as a whole, Morningstar points out that nearly 60% of individual stocks on the index were actually down 20% or more from their all-time highs (1) in August. They also highlight the current volatility of stock prices, with many moving up and down by as much as 20% in just a few months.

Amid the uncertainty and volatility, current stock market conditions may have you wondering whether you should lighten your stock holdings. And if so, where should you invest the proceeds?

For many investors, selling stocks has typically meant moving the proceeds to bonds. Indeed, for those maintaining a portfolio such as the traditional 60/40 weighting of equities to bonds, the current run-up in stock prices and fall in bond prices could mandate a rebalance in this direction to maintain that weighting.

However, some evidence suggests bonds no longer hedge equities (2) — meaning that some investors might start considering how to allocate some of their portfolio to other asset classes.

One move they're making? A growing number of individual investors are adopting alternative assets. According to a survey by Goldman Sachs (3), 39% of individuals with $1 million to $5 million in investable assets are turning to alternatives. That number grows to 80% for those with assets of $10 million or more.

Indeed, about half (49%) of advisors say they're allocating more than 10% of client portfolios to alternatives (4), according to the 2025 CAIS Mercer Survey.

articles.title: New mobile recharge rules: 30-day plans, call-only options and more; TRAI rules explained
articles.summary: Prepaid mobile users will have more recharge options under a new consumer protection framework notified by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
articles.body: Prepaid mobile users will have more recharge options under a new consumer protection framework notified by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), with the changes covering both plan validity and voice-and-SMS-only services.The new rules provide for greater availability of voice-and-SMS-only Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs), including plans valid for 30 days or less. They also provide for a plan that can renew on the same date every month.The changes were highlighted by Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha, who said they addressed concerns he had raised in Parliament earlier this year. His concerns included the 28-day validity offered on several monthly prepaid plans and the lack of voice-only options for consumers who do not require mobile data.What are the new changes?TRAI notified the Telecom Consumers Protection (13th Amendment) Regulations, 2026 on September 22. Under the amended framework, telecom service providers will have to expand the availability of voice-and-SMS-only STVs.These will include options with a validity of 30 days or less. The framework also provides for a voucher that can renew on the same date each month.Another change relates to shorter-duration plans. Where bundled plans are offered for shorter validity periods, telecom service providers will also have to provide corresponding voice-and-SMS-only vouchers. The tariff for these vouchers will have to be reduced appropriately.The new regulations follow a consultation process in which 1,132 responses were received from stakeholders.Why the 30-day validity issue was raisedChadha had earlier questioned why prepaid users were effectively required to recharge 13 times a year when a year has 12 months. He had pointed to the 28-day validity of many monthly plans and sought the introduction of 30-day validity options.“There are 12 months in a year, but prepaid users have to recharge 13 times. Why is there a monthly recharge of 28 days? 30-days validity plans should be introduced” Chadha said, adding that he had called for 30-day validity plans.The issue of plan choice also extended to consumers who use their phones primarily for calls and do not need mobile data. Chadha had sought voice-only prepaid plans for such users, including options that support incoming and outgoing calls.Voice-and-SMS-only plansThe amended framework expands the availability of voice-and-SMS-only STVs. These are prepaid plans that provide voice and SMS services without data and are intended for consumers who do not require internet services, according to TRAI's existing description of such packs.Chadha said the availability of these options would particularly help people who do not need data services, including senior citizens and low-budget users who mainly use their phones for calls.“Many consumers who do not want data but want voice-only plans, prepaid voice-only plans for incoming and outgoing facilities will be made available,” he said.Chadha linked the regulatory changes to the concerns he had raised in Parliament and said the development showed how issues raised by elected representatives, when supported by the public, could lead to regulatory action.“I think this is a perfect example of constructive politics,” he said, adding that he hoped similar efforts would continue to address what he described as the “real problems” faced by people.You use AI every day. articles.title: My husband and I have $250K saved at 59. I thought our retirement plan was solid until I learned my coworker saved $700K
articles.summary: The size of your nest egg is only part of the retirement equation. Here’s what really determines whether your savings are on track.
articles.body:
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.

It's easy to feel confident about your retirement savings — right up until you find out someone your age has put away a lot more.

Comparison can be particularly dangerous when it comes to money. Warren Buffett once made that point to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders: "As an investor, you get something out of all the deadly sins — except for envy," he said in 2010 (1). "Being envious of someone else is pretty stupid."

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

A record 45% of central banks plan to grow gold reserves — and many investors are following suit. Get your free gold IRA guide from Priority Gold

But as retirement gets closer, learning that a friend has accumulated nearly three times as much as you can render such advice meaningless.

Consider a 59-year-old nurse and her husband, who have spent decades preparing for retirement. They have about $250,000 in retirement accounts, another $200,000 to $300,000 in home equity and expect to receive a $1,100 monthly pension.

They're also anticipating somewhere between $1,800 and $2,300 a month in combined Social Security benefits, depending on when they claim.

For years, that seemed like a reasonably solid foundation. Then the nurse learned that a friend earning a similar salary had accumulated $700,000 in a 401(k).

Suddenly, that $250,000 doesn't seem like nearly enough.

But comparing two retirement account balances doesn't tell you whether one household is prepared and another is falling behind. Income, expenses, pensions, Social Security, housing and the age at which you retire can all dramatically change the calculation.

So, how does $250,000 at age 59 compare with what other Americans have saved — and what could this couple do during their remaining working years to strengthen their position?

At first glance, this couple might appear to be well behind their peers.

According to the most recent data from the Federal Reserve (2), Americans between 55 and 64 have an average of $537,560 saved for retirement — more than twice this couple's $250,000.

But averages can be misleading when it comes to wealth because households with very large balances pull the figure higher. The median retirement savings for the same age group is just $185,000 (3).

articles.title: The AI gold rush is fueling a record tech bond boom: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Tech giants are increasingly turning to the bond market for their AI infrastructure build-out.
articles.body:
Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META), Microsoft (MSFT), and Oracle ( ORCL ) are expected to see capital expenditures of roughly $800 billion this year and $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs.

As the costs eat into their cash flow, these tech giants are increasingly turning to the bond market. Through August, US companies have issued $1.9 trillion in bonds, a 30% increase from the same period last year, according to SIFMA data .

At the same time, global bond issuance by AI-linked companies has already surpassed $400 billion this year and is running at an annualized pace above $500 billion, according to a quarterly report from the Institute of International Finance (IIF). US companies accounted for roughly 90% of the total.

While the scale of this year's borrowing binge hasn't yet proved to be a constraint on Big Tech, the bigger question is how capital markets will absorb their growing financing needs.

This flood of new debt has raised a broader question for the bond market: Could it crowd out other bond issuers, sending their prices lower and boosting yields?

The question comes as the global bond market has faced a tumultuous week, with the yield on the 10-year Treasury and 30-year Treasury reaching their highest level since 2007 and 2004 , respectively.

Even Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh acknowledged earlier this month that hyperscaler competition for capital is already playing some role.

"The so-called hyperscalers are out in the market raising funding," Warsh said. "The competition for capital is real, and I think it partly explains the increase in yields," he added.

But so far, researchers have found little evidence to suggest that bond market competition or any so-called crowding-out effect has occurred directly between US Treasurys and AI-linked bonds.

Bonds funding the AI build-out are primarily longer-term, while Treasury issuance has shifted to shorter date maturities, limiting overlap. Treasury buyers and hyperscaler bond buyers also tend to be separate investor groups, said Vishwas Patkar, Morgan Stanley's head of US credit strategy, during a Wednesday IIF briefing.

The share of global bond issuance by nonfinancial corporations has also "remained broadly stable," according to the IIF report.

Earlier this week, asset management firm Pimco said it reached a similar conclusion after finding no statistically significant increase in 10-year Treasury yields around the past six mega AI debt offerings.

But the AI boom can add upward pressure on rates even if investors aren't picking hyperscaler bonds over Treasurys.

articles.title: India’s barrier-free tolling explained: No more stopping as FASTag & number plate recognition will help collect toll automatically
articles.summary: A few years ago, India introduced FASTag to make toll collection across its highways and expressways digital and cashless.
articles.body: A few years ago, India introduced FASTag to make toll collection across its highways and expressways digital and cashless. Now, it is looking to make the process barrier-free or toll plaza free. Imagine zipping through highways and not stopping at toll points, but instead a system that will automatically cut toll from your FASTag.The government is rolling out the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) technology on national highways.Barrier-free tolling is seen as the next step after FASTag. While FASTag made toll payments digital, vehicles still need to slow down and pass through toll lanes and barriers.With barrier-free tolling, vehicles can move through at normal highway speeds while cameras and FASTag systems identify the vehicle and collect the toll automatically.Road Transport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari recently said that the aim is to make toll booths on national highways barrier-free by March 2027. Gadkari has said that over 70% of toll booths will have the MLFF system by December end.According to this TOI report, the Economic Survey 2025-26 had projected a rollout timeline of March 2029 for the MLFF tolling across all National Highways that are four-lane or more, and all high-speed corridors.From FASTag to barrier-free tollingFASTag has become the backbone of electronic toll collection. According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, more than 98% of user-fee collection now takes place through FASTag.The system has also evolved beyond simply automating payment at conventional toll plazas. The government introduced a FASTag-based Annual Pass for non-commercial cars, jeeps and vans from August 15, 2025.For 2026-27, the pass costs Rs 3,075 and allows travel through National Highway and National Expressway fee plazas for one year or up to 200 crossings, whichever comes first.FASTag is now also the payment component of India's shift towards barrier-free tolling.What is a barrier-free tolling system and where has it been implemented?How the system works is simple: With a combination of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), AI analytics, and FASTag-based electronic toll collection, it replaces the conventional physical barriers that currently act as a speed bump on your ride.This allows toll to be charged without vehicles stopping, slowing down or remaining in a designated lane. The system identifies the vehicle that has crossed a chosen point and the toll is automatically deducted from the FASTag and the user gets a message.The technology, however, does not mean drivers can simply pass without having a functioning payment mechanism. Highway users need to maintain sufficient balance in their FASTag accounts.If a FASTag has insufficient balance or is invalid or non-functional, an electronic notice, or e-Notice, is issued for non-payment. The normal user fee has to be paid within 72 hours.If it is not paid within that period, the charge rises to twice the normal user fee for the vehicle category.E-Notices can be accessed and paid through the designated National Highway fee portal, while grievances can also be raised within the prescribed period.If there is a case of non-payment, it can result in FASTag blacklisting and restrictions on certain vehicle-related services through VAHAN.The first major rollout of the new barrier-free tolling system came in May this year at the Chorayasi Toll Plaza on the Surat-Bharuch section of NH-48 in Gujarat.Since then, several sections of national highways have seen the rollout of the new MLFF system.What are the benefits?The current system takes at least 20 seconds to process each toll transaction, while MLFF will let vehicles cross tolling points at 80-85 kmph, eliminating waiting and the need for extra lanes.According to the government, the new system will help reduce travel time and congestion, improve fuel efficiency, lower vehicular emissions and reduce human intervention in toll operations.The system is designed to allow vehicles to move through the tolling point without stopping, thereby reducing waiting and improving traffic flow.According to Gadkari, the full implementation of FASTag will lead to up to Rs 25,000 crore per year to the government."When the system will go fully live, then our department alone would deliver a benefit of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore per year to the Government of India because of the use of FASTags," Gadkari recently said.The government estimates that wider adoption of MLFF could reduce annual toll collection operating costs from nearly 15% to around 3-4%, potentially saving about Rs 5,000-6,000 crore a year. It also estimates annual fuel savings of nearly 250 crore litres and a reduction of around 81,000 tonnes of carbon emissions.Jagannarayan Padmanabhan, Senior Director and Global Head-Consulting, Crisil Intelligence explains that while the basic payment system remains similar, the way toll plazas operate changes significantly. The focus moves from managing booths and queues to managing technology, vehicle identification and digital enforcement.“The biggest benefit of barrier-less plazas will be smoother traffic movement. Vehicles will no longer need to slow down, stop or queue at toll plazas. This can reduce travel time, fuel consumption and congestion, especially on busy highway stretches,” Jagannarayan Padmanabhan tells TOI.Not only that, there can also be savings in the cost of collecting tolls.FASTags have reduced cash handling, but toll plazas still require booths, barriers, manpower, electricity and maintenance.According to Padmanabhan, barrier-free tolling can reduce many of these costs by shifting toll collection to cameras, sensors and centralised digital systems.However, Padmanabhan cautions that the extent of savings realized by concessionaires and operators will ultimately depend on factors such as traffic volumes, technology deployment and maintenance costs, as well as the effectiveness of toll violation enforcement and recovery mechanisms.The CRISIL expert notes that aggregate ETC data from six operational MLFF toll plazas through August 2026 also highlights several noteworthy trends.Of the total ETC collections at MLFF plazas, approximately 6% was recovered through e-notices. During May and June, e-notices accounted for around 12.5% of total transactions and 8.5% of collection value. In comparison, the corresponding figures for July and August moderated to 8.7% of transactions and 5.5% of collections, respectively. “While the operative period remains relatively short, the observed trend suggests an improved efficacy,” he says, adding that the long-term outlook for MLFF tolling remains positive, supported by the government's accelerated rollout plans and the potential for improved network-wide efficiency.“Nevertheless, sustained success will depend on effective management of operational risks, minimization of revenue leakage, and robust enforcement of toll violation penalties to ensure revenue protection and user compliance,” he adds.Raghav Madan, Partner at Deloitte India points out that this will be a significant upgrade over the existing FASTag system.“NHAI has a proven history of implementing new technologies such as FASTag and with the trials of MLFF over the last year, the industry is quite confident this system can be implemented successfully. Rather than solely looking at the financial and economic impact, I see this initiative as another step by NHAI in improving user experience across National Highways, signalling a shift in the organization from “Highway Builder” to “Highway Manager”,” he tells TOI.For you, the biggest visible change will be straightforward: the toll plaza will remain, but the need to stop will disappear. The payment of toll will continue through FASTag, while ANPR will help identify the vehicle as it moves through the tolling point.(With inputs from Dipak K Dash, TNN)You use AI every day. articles.title: Gold and silver outlook: What's in store for traders this week? Job data, crude and more in focus
articles.summary: Gold and silver face another volatile week, with US jobs and inflation data, Federal Reserve signals, Middle East tensions and crude prices set to shape
articles.body: Gold and silver face another volatile week, with US jobs and inflation data, Federal Reserve signals, Middle East tensions and crude prices set to shape bullion sentiment. The holiday-shortened week will put the US non-farm payrolls and unemployment data in focus as markets assess expectations for the Federal Reserve's October policy decision.Consumer confidence, GDP and PCE inflation readings, Eurozone inflation, manufacturing PMIs and speeches from Federal Reserve officials will also provide cues for bullion.The US non-farm payrolls and unemployment data will be closely watched as markets assess expectations around the Federal Reserve's October policy decision. A stronger employment reading could reinforce rate-hike bets and put pressure on gold, while weaker employment data may cool those expectations and support bullion through a softer dollar, Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities, said."The broader outlook remains cautious with volatility likely to stay elevated as the market will closely focus on the upcoming US nonfarm payrolls and unemployment data, which will be crucial in determining expectations around the Federal Reserve's October policy decision," Trivedi said.Markets will also track consumer confidence, GDP and PCE inflation readings from the US, along with Eurozone inflation. Manufacturing PMIs and speeches from Federal Reserve officials are among the other developments expected to provide cues for bullion sentiment.Gold, silver ended lower last weekPrecious metals enter the week after a decline in domestic and international markets.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures for October delivery fell Rs 3,500, or nearly 2.3 per cent, last week to settle at Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams. Silver futures declined Rs 6,907, or 3 per cent, to Rs 2.34 lakh per kilogram."Gold remained highly volatile last week, trading within the Rs 1.5-1.54 lakh per 10 grams range and ending lower by more than 2 per cent as profit booking from higher levels continued as markets increasingly priced in the possibility of another Fed rate hike in October," Trivedi said.The recovery remained limited as traders cut positions at elevated levels.In global markets, Comex gold futures for December delivery dropped $103.7, or 2.34 per cent, last week to $4,321.2 per ounce. Silver fell $2.35, or 3.5 per cent, to $64.80 an ounce in New York."Gold futures traded in a range for most trading sessions last week but overall remained under selling pressure with international prices closing around $4,300 per ounce," said Pranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG - commodity & currency research, JM Financial Services Ltd.Silver futures also ended with a weekly loss following gold and consolidation and correction in industrial metals, he said.Dollar, US bond yields add pressureThe dollar and US Treasury yields will remain important factors for bullion prices.A sustained rise in the dollar index above 101 could add to the pressure on gold, as a stronger dollar tends to reduce demand for dollar-denominated bullion.US 10-year Treasury yields have climbed to their highest since 2007, while 30-year yields are near 2004 highs. Higher long-term yields tend to dent demand for assets such as gold and silver even as Middle East and Russia-Ukraine tensions persist.Middle East and crude in focusGeopolitical uncertainty will continue to play a role, particularly the US-Iran standoff. US President Donald Trump said that he rejected Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in exchange for lifting the naval blockade.Oil markets will offer another variable for bullion and broader commodity sentiment. Russia and Ukraine continue to target energy infrastructure, but higher supplies from Saudi Arabia and Iraq have improved availability this month and weighed on crude prices, Mer said.Commodity markets would remain closed on Friday for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti.You use AI every day. articles.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions linger as Iran and US move further from a deal
articles.summary: There are fears of renewed fighting between the US and Iran, after President Trump rejected a deal.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Hours after US President Donald Trump rejected a diplomatic solution put forward by Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, explosions were heard in the waterway, according to Iranian media.

Reports of blasts near southern Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz suggested that multiple antiship missiles and drones were fired at vessels transiting the waterway against Tehran’s wishes.

While Iranian authorities did not confirm any attacks in the Strait of Hormuz that day, shipping continues to be attacked in the waters, including an Indian cargo ship last week, which killed a sailor .

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) maintains that the strait is closed to any ship that does not coordinate with Iranian authorities. On Sunday afternoon, it released video of what it said was a second US underwater drone seized this month.

Tehran has issued instructions to shipping companies transiting the Strait of Hormuz to use a temporary route approved by Iranian authorities and pay relevant fees. But it has also said the strait will not fully reopen until the US blockade on Iranian ports ends.

Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced on Saturday that it would blacklist any shipping charterer company which orders crews to use routes it considers to be unauthorised.

It also published what it described as an apology from an unnamed shipowner blaming commercial pressure from its charterer for trying to pass through the strait.

Washington still insists that its warships are successfully guiding oil tankers out of the strait via a different route. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News on Sunday that the “running average” of crude oil in transit was nearly 13 million barrels per day.

A September 19 operational update by US Central Command claimed that its forces had helped move more than one billion barrels of crude out of the Gulf over roughly two months.

The US military also says its forces have redirected 122 commercial vessels to enforce the naval blockade of Iran’s ports , halting all Iranian crude exports.

Tehran has claimed that the US is providing false information regarding Strait of Hormuz traffic to project control over the key waterway. Shipping has been severely disrupted since the US and Israel started their war on Iran on February 28.

Andreas Krieg, associate professor at King’s College London, said Iran’s strategy of launching maritime attacks has spread the economic costs of the conflict beyond its borders.

While Iran has suffered economically from war damages, the US naval blockade and sanctions, it would be a mistake “to assume that reaching that threshold produces submission”.

“The next Iranian move is therefore likely to be an attempt to increase the pain experienced by the Gulf rather than simply absorb further American pressure,” Krieg said.

“That could mean more aggressive vessel interdictions in Hormuz, attacks on energy infrastructure, greater Houthi pressure around Bab al-Mandeb and pressure from Iranian-aligned groups against alternative Saudi export routes. We are already seeing how pressure on Hormuz, the Red Sea and Saudi infrastructure can interact.”

At the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Iran projected a message of defiance while also proposing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if its seven conditions were met.

They included lifting the blockade on Iran, the release of frozen Iranian funds and an end to attacks on all fronts, including Israel’s assault on Lebanon. The demands mostly amounted to a return to the June memorandum of understanding between the US and Israel .

Tehran has added that reopening the strait must be undertaken through a bilateral arrangement already finalised with Oman, the only other country with territorial waters in Hormuz.

US President Donald Trump told reporters he rejected the offer, but Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday they were adamant about the conditions and would await an official response through mediators, such as Pakistan, Qatar and Oman.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, chief spokesman of the Iranian armed forces, warned that if the US further intervenes in the Strait of Hormuz, “it will get slapped”.

“The Americans have no way out other than withdrawing from the West Asia region. The sooner they leave, the fewer losses they will incur and the region will certainly become safe after that,” he said.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said conditions were deteriorating so badly for the US that it might launch another “military aggression” on Iran.

Krieg said that as the US moves to isolate Iran via sanctions, Tehran, unable to respond with mutual financial measures against Washington, will be forced to rely on continued coercion in the Strait of Hormuz.

“The most likely level remains controlled attrition rather than an immediate return to the massive air campaign of the opening months,” Krieg said.

“Over the coming weeks, I would expect further attacks or attempted attacks on tankers, US-enabled shipping and regional infrastructure, followed by limited US strikes against IRGC maritime assets, coastal missile positions, drones or vessels involved in those operations. That tit-for-tat cycle has already re-emerged around Hormuz.”

articles.title: US diesel ban: Why cheaper diesel could come with a gasoline price shock
articles.summary: A possible US restriction on diesel exports could have a mixed impact on fuel prices.
articles.body: A possible US restriction on diesel exports could have a mixed impact on fuel prices. Diesel prices in the US could fall at first as more fuel stays in the country, but gasoline prices could later rise if refiners are forced to cut production, Goldman Sachs said.The bank said restrictions on diesel exports, including quotas, were a possible scenario, although it was not its base case. It modelled a possible ban starting in early October and lasting through at least December. A 90-day restriction is reportedly being considered.The impact would first be felt in the US diesel market. With exports restricted, more diesel would remain in the country, pushing up inventories. As long as there is enough storage space, this could put pressure on diesel prices.Goldman Sachs estimates that every week of an export ban could lower average US retail diesel prices by around $0.25 per gallon while storage space remains available.US diesel exports have already increased from 1.1 million barrels per day (mb/d) in 2025 to around 1.6 mb/d in recent months. At the same time, the national average retail diesel price has risen to $6.5 per gallon, according to the report.What happens if diesel storage fills up?The fall in diesel prices may not continue if inventories keep rising and storage space becomes limited.Goldman Sachs estimates that US diesel inventories could theoretically fill up within 9-10 weeks if exports fell by 1.6 mb/d. However, the bank said this could take longer in practice because refiners could reduce production and demand for diesel could increase.Once storage becomes tight, the pressure could shift to refiners.Lower diesel prices could reduce refining margins and encourage refiners to cut output. This could also reduce the amount of gasoline and jet fuel produced.That could push US gasoline prices higher. Goldman Sachs estimates that once diesel storage is full, every additional week of an export ban could put around $0.30 per gallon of upward pressure on US retail gasoline prices.The bank also said gasoline prices could start facing upward pressure even before diesel storage reaches its theoretical limit, as refiners reduce production.Europe could see diesel prices riseThe impact could also be felt outside the US.Goldman Sachs expects diesel prices in Europe and other markets to rise if US exports are restricted. It estimates that every week of an export ban could increase European wholesale diesel prices by around $3 per barrel, or just under 2%.However, releases from European strategic reserves could help limit the increase. Goldman Sachs estimates that these releases could offset around half of the rise.Meanwhile, the effects of a temporary export ban could continue even after restrictions are lifted.Goldman Sachs said US diesel prices would likely reconnect with international prices once the restrictions end. However, global refined-product prices could remain higher than they otherwise would have been because temporary cuts in US refinery output would have reduced inventories.You use AI every day. articles.title: New financing rules are about to make buying or selling a condo even more complicated
articles.summary: Mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are tightening their condo financing policies at a time when the market is still weak.
articles.body:
It hasn't been an easy time to sell a condo , and new financing rules taking effect between now and early 2027 might make it even more complex.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the mortgage giants that support about 70% of the mortgage market, are tightening their standards for acceptable condo financing. "Limited reviews" that allowed many highly qualified buyers to receive mortgages after a cursory look at the financial and structural health of a condo building were eliminated last month, in favor of closer reviews for all but the smallest buildings. And starting in January, Fannie and Freddie will require condo associations to allocate at least 15% of their assessment income toward their reserves, up from 10% today.

The financing changes are part of an ongoing effort to improve condo safety after the deadly collapse of an aging building in Surfside, Fla., in 2021. But they're also a new roadblock in a market that's already seen slumping prices, growing supply, and increased buyer skepticism toward special assessments and monthly fees .

"A well-run, established HOA with solid reserves, acceptable finances, no major items like maintenance or litigation…should still be fine," said Michael Belfor, a mortgage banker and branch manager at American Pacific Mortgage in California. "But it absolutely does create more places for it to fail."

Condos have historically lagged the single-family home market, with prices quicker to drop and slower to rise due to their smaller buyer base. The divide has only deepened in recent years as housing affordability has deteriorated and buyers have begun to balk at association fees that can add hundreds or thousands of dollars a month to a mortgage payment.

To make matters worse, many condo associations have had to aggressively hike monthly fees or levy hefty special assessments to get in compliance with state regulations governing deferred maintenance and reserve funding.

The result? Nationally, condo prices have fallen 2% from peak prices a few years earlier, according to Zillow data. And in some parts of the country, especially Florida, the drop has been far steeper. Prices in Punta Gorda, Fla., have dropped 35% from their September 2022 peak, while Tampa has seen a 24% decline. Elsewhere, the median condo in Austin, Texas, is down 28%, while prices in Denver and Raleigh have fallen more than 16%.

Buyer demand remains weak. Condo sales were down 2.7% in August compared to a year earlier, according to National Association of Realtors data. Single-family home sales saw a smaller 1.1% drop. Nationwide, months of condo supply — a real estate industry measure of how long it would take to sell off all inventory at the current sales pace — sits at a buyer-friendly 6.6 months, while single-family homes are at a more balanced 4.7 months.

articles.title: Made-in-India phones get a PLI push as electronics firms receive Rs 19,091 crore
articles.summary: From making more phones at home to sending them overseas, India's electronics manufacturing push has clocked up a sizeable government payout.
articles.body: From making more phones at home to sending them overseas, India's electronics manufacturing push has clocked up a sizeable government payout. Large-scale electronics manufacturing companies have received Rs 19,090.98 crore in incentives up to June this year, the highest among the sectors covered by the scheme, while the sector has attracted investments worth Rs 20,580.20 crore.Across the 14 PLI schemes launched in 2020, the government has disbursed a total of Rs 36,754 crore to beneficiary companies till June 30 this year, according to data from the department for promotion of industry and internal trade (DPIIT).The large-scale electronics manufacturing (LSEM) scheme was introduced in 2020 to boost domestic mobile phone manufacturing. A total of 32 companies were approved as beneficiaries under the scheme.The scheme was initially meant to run for five years from 2020 to 2025, but its tenure was extended by one year to 2025-26. Smartphone exports from India increased to about $30 billion in 2025-26 from $5.5 billion in 2021-22.India has emerged as the world's second-largest mobile manufacturer, while smartphones have become one of the country's top exported commodities.The government launched the PLI programme for 14 sectors, including electronics and pharmaceuticals, with an approved outlay of Rs 1.91 lakh crore. The schemes were aimed at strengthening manufacturing capabilities, attracting investments, promoting exports, generating employment and reducing import dependence.Under the programme, eligible beneficiary companies receive fiscal incentives on incremental sales over the base year.Pharmaceutical companies received Rs 6,662 crore in incentives up to June this year, while beneficiary firms in food products received Rs 3,271.440 crore. articles.title: IIT Madras-backed deeptech fund raises Rs 453cr in first close
articles.summary: IIT Madras and Unicorn India Ventures’ deeptech fund hits Rs 453 crore first close, investing Rs 55 crore in four startups; one-third capital from overseas.
articles.body: BENGALURU: IIT Madras and venture capital firm Unicorn India Ventures have announced the first close of about Rs 450 crore for their Rs 1,000-crore deeptech fund, with roughly a third of the capital coming from overseas investors. The fund will back capital-intensive startups that can take years to reach commercial scale.IITM Unicorn Frontier Fund I, announced earlier this year with a target corpus of Rs 1,000 crore, has already deployed nearly Rs 55 crore across four companies — quantum startup Quanstra, spacetech firm Hathor Rocket, battery startup Triolt Energy and carbon-capture company Carbelim. Individual cheques have ranged from Rs 10 crore to Rs 20 crore.Bhaskar Majumdar, managing partner at Unicorn India Ventures, told TOI that most of the fund’s capital so far has come from individuals and family offices rather than institutional investors. About a third of the first-close capital has come from overseas investors and the remaining two-thirds from India, he said. IIT Madras alumni have played a significant role in the fundraise, though the fund has not disclosed individual LP names.The fund is targeting its final close by the end of the year. IIT Madras director V Kamakoti said the initial plan was for a much smaller fund, but interest from alumni and investors gave the partners confidence to scale up the vehicle. The fund has closed at Rs 453 crore, against an initial expectation of around Rs 250 crore, he said.The partners are positioning the fund as patient capital for deeptech companies, where commercialisation cycles can stretch far beyond those of software startups. Majumdar said only about 25% of the corpus is expected to be deployed as first cheques, leaving room to back portfolio companies in subsequent rounds.“When any of the four companies today need a next round of Rs 50 crore, we will be there again,” he said. The fund is being built with an eight-to-10-year investment horizon, he added.The long gestation periods are also changing how deeptech companies are valued, Majumdar said. He cited semiconductor and space startups, where a technological milestone such as a tape-out or launch can significantly change a company’s valuation even before meaningful revenue begins to flow. Conventional cash-flow-based valuation frameworks often struggle to capture such businesses, he said.Kamakoti, however, said access to capital is increasingly only one part of the challenge. The next hurdle is getting large Indian companies to become customers of homegrown startups. “What we need today is bigger industries to get from these fellows,” he said, arguing that even relatively small purchase orders can help young companies establish market credibility.Majumdar echoed the view, saying govt agencies have often emerged as first customers for defence and semiconductor startups, while large private enterprises still need to step up adoption.IIT Madras will remain at arm’s length from investment decisions, Kamakoti said. The fund is open to startups across India, with an independent investment process determining which companies receive capital.Kamakoti pointed to Ather Energy as an example of the long-term model IIT Madras hopes to replicate. An investment of roughly Rs 15 lakh made more than a decade ago has grown into a stake valued at about Rs 229 crore, he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India sees 30% increase in Michelin Key hotels in second year of rating here
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Managers of great hotels in India now worry about one thing the chefs there don’t have to lose sleep over — visits by anonymous Michelin
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Managers of great hotels in India now worry about one thing the chefs there don’t have to lose sleep over — visits by anonymous Michelin inspectors to see if a property has earned the stars; if it remains good enough to retain them or move up the ladder from one to two and two to the ultimate three stars.The French tyre MNC, which first started grading restaurants and then hotels in its eponymous guide book exactly a century ago to encourage people to buy the then relatively new concept of cars and drive more, had begun rating hotels in India by giving “Keys” last year.In 2025, India had 36 Michelin Key hotels and now that number has gone up by almost a third to 47 for 2026 — representing 10% of the 470 new hotels across 79 destinations globally that have been given one, two or three stars.In a response to TOI query, a statement from Michelin Guide said: “We do not disclose the total number of properties evaluated by our teams. For (2026) selection, 112 Indian hotels enter the Michelin Guide, including 47 distinguished with one, two or three Keys. Two hotels with three Keys; 15 with two Keys; 30 with one Key and 65 selected hotels.”Taj Falaknuma Palace and Taj Lake Palace have earned three Keys each. Those who have two Keys include Oberoi in Agra, Udaipur and Bandhavgarh; Leela Palace in Delhi and Jaipur; Raffles in Jaipur and Udaipur and The Imperial, Delhi. India’s first luxury hotel, Mumbai's iconic Taj Mahal Tower, has got one Key as has the adjacent Taj Mahal Tower.Many Indian chefs abroad have got Michelin stars. However restaurants in India still await those stars. Asked if it plans to start the rating for the same, the Michelin Guide statement said: “At this stage, we have no information to share on this subject… will communicate in due course should an announcement be made regarding this market.”On rating hotels here, the statement said: “The Michelin Keys in India were awarded following anonymous visits and stays carried out by our inspectors, who are full-time employees of the Michelin group, based on five universal criteria applied in every destination. This anonymity ensures that our teams have the same experience as any other guest. This is why a Michelin Key holds the same value, whether it is awarded to a hotel in India, a ryokan in Japan or a boutique hotel in France.”The selection criteria are: “excellence in architecture and design; quality and consistency of service; overall personality and character; value for price and contribution to neighbourhood. “Hotels awarded one or more Keys do not meet just one of these criteria, but all of them,” it says. While one key represents “a very special stay”, two stands for “exceptional stay” and three for “extraordinary stay.” The French company did not disclose the number of inspectors who came to India or the details of their travels “in order to preserve their anonymity.”Leading chefs and hoteliers in India say many places like Vietnam, Dubai and Thailand took the initiative (read funded) for getting stars for their restaurants. Michelin Guide did not say how its expense for rating the hotels in India last year and this were covered.“India has got some of the best hotels in the world and our cuisine is known globally. Having rated restaurants will give an impetus to food tourism. Indian chefs abroad have stars but Indian eateries don’t have the same. This is something we need to work on as a country, especially as our foreign tourists arrivals remain way below the pre-Covid number even as number of Indians travelling abroad keeps rising,” said a leading hotelier who did not want to be named.“The same way the Michelin Star recognises restaurants for outstanding cooking, the Michelin Key recognises hotels for outstanding stays,” says the company’s website.You use AI every day. articles.title: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri meets US lawmakers; Russia sanctions bill and India-US ties in focus
articles.summary: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri on Sunday met a bipartisan US Congressional delegation led by House Foreign Affairs Committee chairman Brian Mast, as the
articles.body: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri on Sunday met a bipartisan US Congressional delegation led by House Foreign Affairs Committee chairman Brian Mast, as the two sides discussed the recently enacted Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), strategic ties and energy security.The talks also covered the future course of India-US ties, energy security, counter-terrorism, freedom of navigation and other international issues of mutual concern, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, adding that the two sides discussed the entire gamut of the bilateral relationship."Foreign secretary Vikram Misri met a bipartisan US Congressional delegation led by Republican Representative Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee."Jaiswal said the discussions covered the "entire gamut" of India-US relations, including the recently enacted Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA)."Discussions covered the entire gamut of India–US relations, including the recently enacted SRIA legislation and the future trajectory of the relationship. They also exchanged views on international issues of mutual concern, energy security, counter-terrorism and freedom of navigation," the MEA spokesperson noted.SRIA's significance for IndiaThe meeting comes as India continues to assess the implications of the US legislation for countries purchasing Russian oil and gas.The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, or SRIA, provides a statutory framework for expanded sanctions, import duties and trade restrictions concerning Russia, while also extending economic measures relating to Iran.The legislation covers Russia's petroleum and military sectors, government officials, financial institutions and vessels associated with efforts to circumvent restrictions on Russian crude exports.For India, a key provision is the mechanism that could allow Washington to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from countries that continue purchasing Russian energy.Such tariffs would be subject to the conditions set out in the legislation and any subsequent invocation by US President Donald Trump.The legislation does not automatically impose a 100 per cent tariff on Indian goods. It instead gives the US executive branch the authority to impose such tariffs under specified conditions.Misri's meetings in New YorkThe latest meeting followed Misri's engagements in New York on Friday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).His discussions there covered critical and emerging technologies, Pax Silica, semiconductors, critical minerals, energy security, civil nuclear cooperation and SRIA.Misri met US under secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg and discussed cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, semiconductors and critical minerals."Great to meet under secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg in New York. Agreed to advance India–US cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, including through Pax Silica, and strengthen cooperation in semiconductors and critical minerals," Misri said.He also held talks with US under secretary of state for political affairs Allison Hooker on energy security and other strategic issues."A productive meeting with US under secretary of state for political affairs Allison Hooker in New York today. Discussed various elements of India-US bilateral cooperation, including energy security and the recently enacted SRIA, civil nuclear cooperation, TRUST and the Indian Ocean Strategic Venture initiative," he said.Trade talks and strategic cooperationThe meetings come as India and the US continue negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).At the same time, the two countries are expanding cooperation in areas considered strategically important to economic and national security, including supply-chain resilience, advanced technologies and energy.Pax Silica, launched by Helberg in December 2025, is the US State Department's flagship initiative focused on AI and supply-chain security.The initiative seeks to build cooperation among partner countries around secure and innovative supply chains spanning critical minerals, energy inputs, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and AI infrastructure.You use AI every day. articles.title: Niño Becerra y el precios de los alimentos: "El gasto en ocio en España está a la par de lo que las familias dedican a alimentación y vivienda"
articles.standfirst: El profesional en la materia asegura que los costes llevan meses disparados
articles.summary: El profesional en la materia asegura que los costes llevan meses disparados
articles.body: Santiago Niño Becerra ha hecho una amplia reflexión sobre el precio de la alimentación y su peso dentro de los gastos de los hogares. El economista ha recurrido a sus redes sociales para analizar cómo ha evolucionado el coste de los alimentos durante los últimos años y compararlo con otro tipo de desembolsos, como los relacionados con el ocio. Su análisis parte de una situación que afecta directamente al bolsillo de los consumidores. Según los datos que comparte Niño Becerra, los precios de la alimentación han experimentado un incremento considerable desde 2021, algo que, en su opinión, está provocando cambios en los hábitos de compra de las familias. “Los precios de la alimentación llevan meses disparados: si en septiembre del 2021 el índice de precios alimentarios era 100, en agosto del 2026 es 134,8, luego ‘el consumidor entra en ‘modo control’: más visitas al súper, más legumbres y menos pescado”, ha escrito el economista en su cuenta de X. A partir de ahí, Niño Becerra introduce el gasto en ocio como elemento de comparación. “Pero la Encuesta de Presupuestos Familiares que publica el INE dice que el 24% del gasto en consumo de los hogares se dirige a ‘Ocio’ (lo que genera el 7,8% del PIB), y concretamente a ‘Bares, menús del día, salidas a cenar los fines de semana y comida a domicilio’ entre el 12% y el 18%”, añade. “El gasto en ‘Ocio’ en España está a la par de lo que, en términos medios, las familias dedican a alimentación y a vivienda. En Europa el gasto en ‘Ocio’ ocupa el cuarto lugar en el gasto doméstico. (Gemini). En los años 2025 y 2026, en términos medios, el gasto en ‘Ocio’ por hogar se situó en 5.600 €, aunque en términos reales se ha producido una caída con respecto a los años 2022 a 2024”, puntualiza.
